question: The Danes sold all their Indian settlements to the British in which year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1845.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Danes, who could not strengthen their position in India, sold all their settlements, including Tranquebar and Serampore, to the British in 1845 (1845 में डेनों ने अपनी सभी बस्तियाँ अंग्रेज़ों को बेच दीं)

 

• Their company had been established in 1616 and its first factory came in 1620 at Tranquebar.

 

• The Danish East India Company was weak in capital and received little government backing, unlike the English and Dutch companies.

 

• With the sale, Danish colonial activity in India came to a formal end after more than two centuries.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Danes were the fourth company to enter India's trade.

 

• The sale ended a Danish presence of about 225 years in the subcontinent.

 

• The Portuguese continued in Goa and the French in Pondicherry even after this sale.

 

• The sale was made by the Danish crown after it decided that its small Indian colonies were unprofitable and difficult to defend.

 

NOTE

 

• 1757 (Option 1): 1757 is the date of Plassey and the capture of Chandernagore from the French, which had nothing to do with Danish settlements.

 

• 1760 (Option 2): 1760 is the year of the Battle of Wandiwash, which broke French power in the south; Danish settlements were untouched by it.

 

• 1858 (Option 3): 1858 is the year of the Government of India Act transferring power from the Company to the Crown, which came after the Danish sale of 1845.

question: The French East India Company was established in 1664 by
solution_text:
The correct answer is Colbert.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• French EIC set up in 1664 by Colbert, the finance minister of Louis XIV (1664 में लुई चौदहवें के मंत्री कोल्बर्ट ने फ्रांसीसी कंपनी बनाई)

 

• It was a state-supported company, with the government supplying much of the capital.

 

• The French were the last of the major European powers to arrive in India.

 

• Their later struggle with the English (the Carnatic wars) ended in French failure.

 

• Colbert gave the company a monopoly of French trade east of the Cape of Good Hope, and the king and nobles were encouraged to invest in its shares.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Colbert's company was called Compagnie des Indes Orientales.

 

• Dupleix, governor of Pondicherry from 1742, led the French during the Carnatic Wars with the British.

 

• The Treaty of Paris (1763) left the French with trading posts only.

 

• The French company had a weak financial position and was reorganised several times, and its exclusive trade rights were suspended in 1769.

 

NOTE

 

• Richelieu (Option 1): Richelieu was the chief minister of Louis XIII earlier in the century and he encouraged colonial companies, but the 1664 company was Colbert's creation.

 

• Dupleix (Option 2): Dupleix came to India as a company official and governor of Pondicherry in the 1740s and could not found a company in 1664.

 

• Napoleon (Option 4): Napoleon ruled France in the early nineteenth century, long after the formation of the French East India Company. He had no connection with the commercial companies of the seventeenth century.

question: The first French factory in India was set up in 1668 at Surat by
solution_text:
The correct answer is Francis Caron.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Francis Caron set up the first French factory in India at Surat in 1668, a few years after the French company was formed (1668 में फ्रांसिस कैरन ने सूरत में पहली फ्रांसीसी फैक्ट्री बनाई)

 

• Caron was a Dutch-born man who had served the Dutch company before joining the French.

 

• The French followed up in 1669 with a factory at Masulipatnam.

 

• Surat was the main European meeting point in Gujarat, where the English had also had a factory since 1613.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pondicherry was bought from the Bijapur governor in 1673-74 by Francois Martin and became the French headquarters.

 

• Chandernagore (1690-92) in Bengal was another major French post.

 

• The last French possessions, such as Pondicherry, were transferred to India in 1954.

 

• Caron had earlier worked for the Dutch East India Company in Japan and Java, and then moved to the French service after a dispute with the Dutch.

 

NOTE

 

• Francois Martin (Option 1): Francois Martin founded Pondicherry in 1674 and became its first governor, which was after the Surat factory. Pondicherry was the later headquarters of the French and was established well after the first factory.

 

• Joseph Dupleix (Option 3): Joseph Francois Dupleix was an eighteenth-century governor of Pondicherry (1742-54), long after the 1668 factory was started. Dupleix is associated with the Carnatic Wars, not with the first French factory.

 

• Count de Lally (Option 4): Count de Lally led French forces in India in 1758-61 and was defeated at Wandiwash in 1760, a century after Caron's Surat factory.

question: Pondicherry, which became the chief French settlement in India, was founded in 1674 by
solution_text:
The correct answer is Francois Martin.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Francois Martin founded Pondicherry in about 1674 on the Coromandel coast, acquiring the site from the Bijapur governor of the region, and became its first governor (1674 में फ्रांसुआ मार्टिन ने पांडिचेरी की नींव रखी)

 

• Pondicherry developed into the capital of French India and the base of operations during the Carnatic Wars.

 

• French commerce had started earlier at Surat (1668) with the work of Francis Caron.

 

• The French company itself had been founded in 1664 by Colbert.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pondicherry became the seat of the French governor, such as Dupleix, in the next century.

 

• The Battle of Wandiwash (1760) and the fall of Pondicherry (1761) broke French power.

 

• France handed over Pondicherry, Karaikal, Mahe and Yanam to India after independence.

 

• Under Dupleix, who governed from 1742, Pondicherry became the centre of French political ambition in south India.

 

NOTE

 

• Francis Caron (Option 1): Francis Caron began the French trade at Surat in 1668 and is not the founder of Pondicherry, which was developed by his successor in the 1670s.

 

• Colbert (Option 2): Colbert was a minister in Paris who created the company but never visited India or founded a settlement there. Colbert's role was the formation of the company in Paris, not the founding of any Indian settlement.

 

• Robert Clive (Option 4): Robert Clive was an English Company official whose career began in the 1740s, so he could not have founded the French settlement in 1674.

question: Fort St George at Madras was founded by the English in 1639 under the leadership of
solution_text:
The correct answer is Francis Day.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Francis Day obtained a strip of land on the Coromandel coast in 1639 from the local Nayak ruler and built Fort St George, around which Madras grew (फ्रांसिस डे ने 1639 में मद्रास में फोर्ट सेंट जॉर्ज बनवाया)

 

• Fort St George was the first major English fortified settlement in the south.

 

• It later became the headquarters of the Madras Presidency.

 

• Madras, with Bombay and Calcutta, formed the three presidency towns.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The grant came with the permission of the Raja of Chandragiri, who ruled the area.

 

• Fort St George was the first fort built by the British East India Company in India.

 

• Madras replaced Masulipatnam as the main English centre on the Coromandel coast.

 

• Madras was initially called Madraspatam, and in 1640 the Company moved its Coromandel headquarters there from Masulipatnam.

 

NOTE

 

• Job Charnock (Option 2): Job Charnock founded Calcutta in 1690 in Bengal, not Madras in the south. Charnock's settlement was on the Hugli in the north-east, not on the Coromandel coast.

 

• Gerald Aungier (Option 3): Gerald Aungier was the governor of Bombay (1669-77), who developed that city and not Madras. Aungier's work was in western India, so he cannot be linked with a fort built on the southeastern coast.

 

• Thomas Roe (Option 4): Sir Thomas Roe was the ambassador at Jahangir's court in 1615-19, who secured trading permissions in the north and did not build Fort St George.

question: Arrange the European powers in the order of their arrival in India (earliest first):
solution_text:
The correct answer is Portuguese, Dutch, English, Danish, French.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The notes give the sequence Portuguese (1498), Dutch (1605), English (1608), Danish (1616) and French (1664) (आगमन क्रम: पुर्तगाली, डच, अंग्रेज़, डेन, फ्रांसीसी)

 

• The Portuguese came first through Vasco da Gama's arrival at Calicut in 1498.

 

• The Dutch established their first factory at Masulipatnam in 1605, and the English company (formed 1600) set up Surat in 1613, with Hawkins arriving in 1608.

 

• The Danish company was founded in 1616 and the French company in 1664, which makes the French the last.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Companies were formed in the order English (1600), Dutch (1602), Danish (1616), French (1664).

 

• Portuguese were the first to arrive and the last to leave (1961).

 

• The sequence is a regular feature of SSC and state-level exams.

 

• The Portuguese, Dutch, English and French came from Atlantic Europe, but only the Portuguese took the Cape route in the earliest wave.

 

NOTE

 

• Portuguese, English, Dutch, French, Danish (Option 1): This order puts the English before the Dutch and the French before the Danes, which is the reverse of the actual sequence of arrival in India.

 

• Dutch, Portuguese, English, Danish, French (Option 3): This option places the Dutch at the start, ahead of the Portuguese, although Vasco da Gama's arrival in 1498 preceded all other European powers by over a century.

 

• Portuguese, Dutch, Danish, English, French (Option 4): This arrangement lists the Danes before the English; the Danish company came in 1616, after the English had already reached the Mughal court in 1608.

question: Arrange these Portuguese and English events in chronological order:
option_1: Albuquerque captures Goa - Vasco da Gama reaches Calicut - Battle of Swally - Bombay given to Charles II as dowry
option_2: Vasco da Gama reaches Calicut - Battle of Swally - Albuquerque captures Goa - Bombay given to Charles II as dowry
option_3: Vasco da Gama reaches Calicut - Albuquerque captures Goa - Battle of Swally - Bombay given to Charles II as dowry
option_4: Vasco da Gama reaches Calicut - Albuquerque captures Goa - Bombay given to Charles II as dowry - Battle of Swally
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vasco da Gama reaches Calicut - Albuquerque captures Goa - Battle of Swally - Bombay given to Charles II as dowry.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vasco da Gama reached Calicut in 1498, the earliest event in the list (वास्को डी गामा 1498, गोवा 1510, स्वाली 1612, बम्बई दहेज 1662)

 

• Albuquerque captured Goa from Bijapur in 1510.

 

• The English defeated the Portuguese at Swally in 1612.

 

• Bombay passed to the English crown as the dowry of Catherine of Braganza in 1662, the last event.

 

• Each of these events moved the European presence further: from first contact, to territory, to naval success, to the acquisition of an island.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Between Gama and the Swally battle, the Portuguese had a 114-year period of monopoly.

 

• Charles II leased the dowry island to the Company in 1668.

 

• The Portuguese were reduced to Goa, Diu and Daman in the seventeenth century.

 

• Between Gama's landing and the first English factory, the Portuguese enjoyed a monopoly of the Cape route for over a century, which ended with Dutch and English competition in the early 1600s.

 

NOTE

 

• Albuquerque captures Goa - Vasco da Gama reaches Calicut - Battle of Swally - Bombay given to Charles II as dowry (Option 1): This order shows Goa captured before Gama's arrival, which is impossible since the Portuguese reached India in 1498 and took Goa in 1510.

 

• Vasco da Gama reaches Calicut - Battle of Swally - Albuquerque captures Goa - Bombay given to Charles II as dowry (Option 2): This order places Swally ahead of Goa, but the Goa conquest of 1510 came more than a century before the naval fight of 1612.

 

• Vasco da Gama reaches Calicut - Albuquerque captures Goa - Bombay given to Charles II as dowry - Battle of Swally (Option 4): This order puts the Bombay dowry before Swally; the marriage of 1662 followed the naval battle of 1612 by half a century.

question: Arrange these English-Mughal events in chronological order:
option_1: Roe's embassy - Hawkins at Jahangir's court - Lease of Bombay to the Company - English factory on the Hugli
option_2: Hawkins at Jahangir's court - Roe's embassy - English factory on the Hugli - Lease of Bombay to the Company
option_3: Hawkins at Jahangir's court - English factory on the Hugli - Roe's embassy - Lease of Bombay to the Company
option_4: Roe's embassy - Hawkins at Jahangir's court - English factory on the Hugli - Lease of Bombay to the Company
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hawkins at Jahangir's court - Roe's embassy - English factory on the Hugli - Lease of Bombay to the Company.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• William Hawkins appeared at Jahangir's court in 1609, the first of the four events (हॉकिन्स 1609, रो 1615, हुगली 1651, बम्बई पट्टा 1668)

 

• Sir Thomas Roe arrived in 1615 and stayed until 1619.

 

• The English factory on the Hugli in Bengal came in 1651.

 

• The lease of Bombay to the Company by Charles II was in 1668.

 

• The four steps show the early English approach: diplomacy with the Mughal court, then regional concessions, and finally an island base of their own.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hawkins was given a mansab of 400 and the title English Khan.

 

• Hugli in 1651 was made possible by Shah Shuja's farman.

 

• Fort William in 1700 was next, following the 1690 foundation of Calcutta.

 

• After 1615 Roe's presence at the Mughal court made Agra a base for English trade, while the Bengal expansion came decades later with Shah Shuja's concession.

 

NOTE

 

• Roe's embassy - Hawkins at Jahangir's court - Lease of Bombay to the Company - English factory on the Hugli (Option 1): This sequence begins with Roe, whereas Hawkins's failed mission (1609) preceded Roe's successful one (1615), and it also puts the Bombay lease of 1668 ahead of the Hugli factory of 1651.

 

• Hawkins at Jahangir's court - English factory on the Hugli - Roe's embassy - Lease of Bombay to the Company (Option 3): This sequence puts the Hugli factory of 1651 ahead of Roe's embassy of 1615, though the first two events are right, so the third place is wrongly filled by a later event.

 

• Roe's embassy - Hawkins at Jahangir's court - English factory on the Hugli - Lease of Bombay to the Company (Option 4): This sequence starts with Roe's embassy, although Hawkins had already come to Jahangir's court in 1609, six years before Roe arrived in 1615.

question: Arrange the following in chronological order of establishment:
option_1: Danish East India Company - Dutch East India Company - French East India Company - Danish colony at Serampore
option_2: Dutch East India Company - Danish East India Company - Danish colony at Serampore - French East India Company
option_3: Dutch East India Company - Danish East India Company - French East India Company - Danish colony at Serampore
option_4: French East India Company - Dutch East India Company - Danish East India Company - Danish colony at Serampore
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dutch East India Company - Danish East India Company - French East India Company - Danish colony at Serampore.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Dutch company was set up in 1602 (डच कंपनी 1602, डेनिश 1616, फ्रांसीसी 1664, सीरामपुर 1755)

 

• The Danish company followed in 1616.

 

• The French company came into existence under Colbert in 1664.

 

• The Danes established a colony at Serampore in 1755, the last in the list.

 

• The order shows that the Dutch and Danish companies were formed before the French one and that a colony at Serampore came much later.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The English company (1600) was formed before all these.

 

• The Danes sold Serampore and Tranquebar in 1845.

 

• The Danes had earlier built a factory at Tranquebar in 1620.

 

• The Danes and French both entered the field much later than the Portuguese and English, which explains their limited successes.

 

• The Danish and Dutch companies were mainly commercial, whereas the French company was set up by the state.

 

NOTE

 

• Danish East India Company - Dutch East India Company - French East India Company - Danish colony at Serampore (Option 1): This order puts the Danish company before the Dutch one, though the VOC was set up in 1602 and the Danish company only in 1616.

 

• Dutch East India Company - Danish East India Company - Danish colony at Serampore - French East India Company (Option 2): This order puts Serampore before the French company, while the Danish colony of 1755 followed the French company of 1664 by almost a century.

 

• French East India Company - Dutch East India Company - Danish East India Company - Danish colony at Serampore (Option 4): This order starts with the French company, which was the latest of the three companies, formed in 1664. A chronological list cannot start with the latest of the companies.

question:
Match the following:

Column A: (a) Portuguese (b) Dutch (c) Danish (d) French

Column B: (i) Masulipatnam (ii) Tranquebar (iii) Surat (iv) Goa
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Portuguese centre was Goa (iv), captured in 1510 and made capital in 1530 (पुर्तगाली-गोवा, डच-मसूलीपट्टनम, डेन-ट्रांकेबार, फ्रांसीसी-सूरत)

 

• The Dutch founded their first factory at Masulipatnam (i) in 1605.

 

• The Danes began at Tranquebar (ii) in 1620.

 

• The French established their first factory at Surat (iii) in 1668 under Francis Caron.

 

• The pairing links each European power with the place that served as its first or main settlement in the notes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Surat was also the English permanent factory site (1613).

 

• Masulipatnam hosted the first English factory (1611) as well.

 

• Goa was the capital of Portuguese India until 1961.

 

• The Portuguese retained Daman and Diu in Gujarat, but their main seat was always in Goa.

 

• The French also held Chandernagore in Bengal from 1690, apart from Surat and Pondicherry.

 

NOTE

 

• a-i, b-iv, c-ii, d-iii (Option 1): This pairing gives Goa to the Dutch and Masulipatnam to the Portuguese, a reversal of the actual positions of the two powers.

 

• a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii (Option 3): This pairing makes Tranquebar a Dutch place and Masulipatnam a Danish one, which mixes up two coastal centres. The Danes were at Tranquebar and the Dutch at Masulipatnam, which is what the correct pairing shows.

 

• a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv (Option 4): This pairing gives Surat to the Portuguese and Goa to the French, but the French reached Surat in 1668 and never held Goa.

question:
Match the following:

Column A: (a) Francisco de Almeida (b) Alfonso de Albuquerque (c) Nino da Cunha (d) Thomas Best

Column B: (i) Capital moved to Goa (ii) Blue Water Policy (iii) Victory at Swally (iv) Real founder of Portuguese power
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Almeida is associated with the Blue Water Policy (ii) (अल्मेडा-ब्लू वाटर, अल्बुकर्क-वास्तविक संस्थापक, कुन्हा-राजधानी गोवा, बेस्ट-स्वाली)

 

• Albuquerque is the real founder of Portuguese power (iv), who took Goa in 1510.

 

• Nino da Cunha moved the capital to Goa (i) in 1530.

 

• Thomas Best won at Swally (iii) in 1612.

 

• Each person in Column A held a different place in the Portuguese or English story, and the match uses the main distinguishing achievement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Almeida's was the shortest reign among the three Portuguese leaders (1505-09).

 

• Cunha also founded a Hooghly factory.

 

• Best's victory was followed by the Surat factory of 1613.

 

• Almeida's son Lourenco was killed in 1508, and Almeida avenged him in the sea battle at Diu in 1509.

 

• Albuquerque's rule saw Portuguese expansion to Malacca and Hormuz, while Cunha's saw Bassein and Diu.

 

NOTE

 

• a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii (Option 2): This set swaps Almeida's and Albuquerque's roles, giving the founder title to Almeida, who was the first Viceroy with a naval strategy.

 

• a-ii, b-i, c-iv, d-iii (Option 3): This set gives the capital shift to Albuquerque and the founder label to Cunha, which reverses the real order of their contributions.

 

• a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i (Option 4): This set gives Swally to Cunha and the capital shift to Best, mixing a Portuguese governor with an English captain. Best was not Portuguese and Cunha was not English, so the pairing cannot hold.

question:
Match the following:

Column A: (a) Ralph Fitch (b) William Hawkins (c) Thomas Roe (d) Francis Day

Column B: (i) Fort St George (ii) Ship Hector (iii) Akbar's court (iv) Factories at Agra and Broach
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ralph Fitch visited Akbar's court (iii) about 1583 (फिच-अकबर का दरबार, हॉकिन्स-हेक्टर, रो-आगरा-ब्रोच, डे-फोर्ट सेंट जॉर्ज)

 

• William Hawkins sailed in the ship Hector (ii) in 1608.

 

• Thomas Roe secured factories at Agra, Ahmedabad and Broach (iv) by 1619.

 

• Francis Day built Fort St George (i) at Madras in 1639.

 

• Each name in Column A is connected with a different step in the English approach to Mughal India, from the first merchant to the Madras founder.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hawkins met Jahangir, since Akbar had died in 1605.

 

• Roe stayed for three years at Jahangir's court.

 

• Fort St George became the nucleus of Madras city.

 

• Fitch's travels were recorded in Hakluyt's collection of voyages.

 

• Hawkins's journey was recorded in his own narrative, and Roe's in his journal.

 

NOTE

 

• a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i (Option 1): This set gives Hector to Fitch and Akbar's court to Hawkins, but Hawkins arrived in the reign of Jahangir, and Fitch came before the Company existed.

 

• a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i (Option 2): This set gives the Hector to Roe and the factories to Hawkins, which is wrong since Hawkins failed in obtaining permission.

 

• a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv (Option 3): This set gives Fort St George to Roe and the factories to Day, reversing the roles of the ambassador and the Madras founder.

question:
Match the following:

Column A: (a) 1498 (b) 1602 (c) 1616 (d) 1664

Column B: (i) Danish company formed (ii) French company formed (iii) Vasco da Gama at Calicut (iv) Dutch company formed
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 1498 marks Vasco da Gama's arrival at Calicut (iii) (1498-गामा, 1602-डच कंपनी, 1616-डेनिश कंपनी, 1664-फ्रांसीसी कंपनी)

 

• 1602 saw the founding of the Dutch East India Company (iv).

 

• 1616 is the year of the Danish East India Company (i).

 

• 1664 is the year of the French East India Company (ii), set up by Colbert.

 

• The dates are the main milestones: Gama's arrival, then the three company foundations of 1602, 1616 and 1664.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The English company dates from 31 December 1600.

 

• The first Dutch factory in India, at Masulipatnam, was in 1605.

 

• The first Danish factory, at Tranquebar, was in 1620.

 

• The English company founded in 1600 is the earliest of the companies, though it arrived in Indian trade after the Dutch factory of 1605.

 

• The English company, formed in 1600, belongs to the earlier group of companies and is therefore not part of this list of dates.

 

NOTE

 

• a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii (Option 2): This pairing gives 1498 to the Dutch company and 1602 to Gama, which mixes the first European voyage with a company formed more than a century later.

 

• a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii (Option 3): This pairing gives 1602 to the Danes and 1616 to the Dutch, switching the two companies and putting the Dutch after the Danes.

 

• a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i (Option 4): This pairing gives 1616 to the French company and 1664 to the Danish one, swapping the two latest dates between the two powers.

question:
Match the following settlements with the European power:

Column A: (a) Chinsurah (b) Serampore (c) Pondicherry (d) Daman

Column B: (i) French (ii) Danish (iii) Portuguese (iv) Dutch
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chinsurah on the Hugli was a Dutch (iv) settlement (चिनसुरा-डच, सीरामपुर-डेनिश, पांडिचेरी-फ्रांसीसी, दमन-पुर्तगाली)

 

• Serampore was the Danish headquarters from 1755, a Danish (ii) colony.

 

• Pondicherry was the French (i) headquarters founded in 1674.

 

• Daman remained a Portuguese (iii) territory until 1961.

 

• The pairing is based on the main colonial settlement of each power, three in the east coast and Bengal belt and one on the west coast.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chinsurah was exchanged by the Dutch with the British in 1825 for Sumatra possessions.

 

• Pondicherry, Karaikal, Mahe and Yanam were French until 1954.

 

• Goa, Daman and Diu were the Portuguese possessions taken in 1961.

 

• Chinsurah was exchanged in 1825 for the Dutch possessions in Sumatra under the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824.

 

• Daman and Diu are in present-day Gujarat, near Surat's coast.

 

NOTE

 

• a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii (Option 1): This pairing gives Chinsurah to the Danes and Serampore to the Dutch, exchanging two Hugli-side towns that belonged to two different powers.

 

• a-iv, b-ii, c-iii, d-i (Option 2): This pairing makes Pondicherry Portuguese and Daman French, though the French base was on the Coromandel coast and Daman is on the Gujarat coast.

 

• a-i, b-ii, c-iv, d-iii (Option 4): This pairing makes Chinsurah French and Pondicherry Dutch, a mix-up of the two Coromandel and Bengal headquarters. This is not how the Dutch and French settlements are really placed.

question:
Assertion (A): After 1612 the English became the leading European power in India's sea trade, replacing the Portuguese.

Reason (R): Captain Thomas Best defeated the Portuguese fleet at the Battle of Swally.
option_1: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_2: A is true but R is false
option_3: A is false but R is true
option_4: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion A is true: the Portuguese lost their dominant position and the English emerged as the leading European trading power on the western coast (1612 के बाद अंग्रेज़ पुर्तगालियों की जगह प्रमुख शक्ति बने)

 

• Reason R is true: Captain Thomas Best defeated the Portuguese in the Battle of Swally (Suvali) in 1612 off Surat.

 

• R explains A, since the naval victory proved English strength and led to the establishment of the Surat factory in 1613.

 

• The Mughal officials also became more willing to deal with the English once Portuguese naval superiority was broken.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Portuguese decline had begun after 1600 because of Dutch and English attacks on their commerce.

 

• Sir Thomas Roe's embassy (1615-19) built on the goodwill gained at Swally.

 

• Later Portuguese strength was limited to Goa, Diu and Daman.

 

• Portuguese naval power was seriously reduced after the English victory, and the Portuguese asked the Mughal governor to expel the English from Surat, but without success.

 

NOTE

 

• Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A (Option 1): R is a true statement that explains A, so it is not just an independent fact; the naval defeat is the direct cause of the English rise.

 

• A is true but R is false (Option 2): A is true, since the notes and textbooks say the English replaced the Portuguese after Swally, so describing it as false is incorrect.

 

• A is false but R is true (Option 3): R is also true as the victory is credited to Thomas Best, which means the option calling R false is rejected.

question:
Assertion (A): King Charles II leased Bombay to the East India Company in 1668.

Reason (R): Bombay had been acquired by the English crown as part of the dowry of Catherine of Braganza.
option_1: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_2: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
option_3: A is true but R is false
option_4: A is false but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion A is true: in 1668 Charles II leased Bombay to the Company for ten pounds a year (1668 में चार्ल्स द्वितीय ने बम्बई कंपनी को पट्टे पर दी)

 

• Reason R is true: Bombay came to the Crown in 1662 through the marriage of Charles II with Catherine of Braganza.

 

• R explains A: only because the Crown owned the island could the king lease it to the Company.

 

• The Crown found it difficult to administer an island far from England, so handing it over was convenient.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The island had earlier belonged to the Portuguese and was ceded to England in a treaty in 1661.

 

• Bombay's harbour was later more important than Surat for the Company.

 

• It became the headquarters of the Bombay Presidency.

 

• The Treaty of 1661 between England and Portugal also made Portugal's possessions in Asia safe from Dutch attack with English help.

 

NOTE

 

• Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A (Option 1): R gives the reason for the lease, as the king could lease only what he held, so the two are not unrelated facts.

 

• A is true but R is false (Option 3): A is correct, because the 1668 lease is recorded in the notes, and it cannot be called false. The lease was recorded in 1668, so A is not false.

 

• A is false but R is true (Option 4): R is also true, since the dowry is documented as the means by which England obtained Bombay. The dowry transfer of 1662 is the basis of R, which is why R is not false.

question:
Assertion (A): The Portuguese stayed in India longer than any other European power.

Reason (R): Goa, Diu and Daman were taken over by India in 1947.
option_1: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
option_2: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_3: A is false but R is true
option_4: A is true but R is false
solution_text:
The correct answer is A is true but R is false.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion A is true: the Portuguese came first (1498) and stayed the longest, till 1961 (पुर्तगाली सबसे पहले आए और सबसे अंत तक रहे)

 

• Reason R is false: the British left in 1947, but Goa, Diu and Daman remained Portuguese and were taken by India in 1961.

 

• French territories such as Pondicherry were transferred in 1954, earlier than Portuguese Goa.

 

• Since R carries a wrong date, it cannot be a valid explanation of A.

 

• The Portuguese were the first European power to arrive in India and the last to leave, as their rule lasted from 1498 to 1961.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Operation Vijay of December 1961 ended Portuguese rule in Goa.

 

• The French colonies were merged de facto in 1954 and de jure in 1962.

 

• The Portuguese had been reduced to three enclaves by the end of the seventeenth century.

 

• India's Constitution (Twelfth Amendment, 1962) incorporated Goa, Daman and Diu as a Union Territory after the 1961 action.

 

NOTE

 

• Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A (Option 1): A is true and R is false, so the claim that both are true is wrong, because 1947 was the year of British departure and not of the Portuguese exit.

 

• Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A (Option 2): R is not a correct explanation and not a true statement, so a pair with both true is wrong even if A is correctly stated.

 

• A is false but R is true (Option 3): A is true because the Portuguese remained until 1961, which makes the option calling A false incorrect. The Portuguese stayed until 1961, so A is not false.

question:
Assertion (A): Alfonso de Albuquerque is regarded as the real founder of Portuguese power in India.

Reason (R): He captured Goa from the Bijapur Sultan in 1510 and made it the base of Portuguese rule.
option_1: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_2: A is true but R is false
option_3: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
option_4: A is false but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion A is true: Albuquerque, governor from 1509 to 1515, laid the foundation of a lasting Portuguese empire in the East (अल्बुकर्क पुर्तगाली सत्ता का वास्तविक संस्थापक)

 

• Reason R is true: in 1510 he took Goa from the Adil Shahi Sultan of Bijapur.

 

• R explains A, since Goa gave the Portuguese a territorial base rather than just ships and coastal forts.

 

• His predecessor Almeida had relied on naval power and the Blue Water Policy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Albuquerque seized Malacca in 1511 and Hormuz in 1515.

 

• His policy of marriage with Indian women created a mixed community in Goa.

 

• Goa remained the Portuguese capital until the end of their rule in 1961.

 

• Albuquerque's lasting contributions included a chain of forts and an administrative base at Goa, and he also discouraged the trade of slaves in some ports.

 

NOTE

 

• Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A (Option 1): R is not an independent statement, since the conquest of Goa is the main reason for the founder title, so calling it an unrelated truth is wrong.

 

• A is true but R is false (Option 2): A is true because textbooks say Albuquerque is the real founder, so a claim that A is false is rejected. This view ignores the standard textbook position.

 

• A is false but R is true (Option 4): R is true as the capture of Goa in 1510 is established in history, so the claim that R is false is not valid.

question:
Consider the following statements about Vasco da Gama:

1. He reached the Cape of Good Hope in November 1497.

2. He landed at Calicut in May 1498.

3. He never returned to India after his first voyage.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Gama reached the Cape of Good Hope on 22 November 1497 (गामा 22 नवंबर 1497 को उत्तमाशा अंतरीप पहुँचा)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: he landed at Calicut on 20 May 1498, where the Zamorin was the ruler.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: Gama returned to Portugal in 1499 and visited India again in 1502.

 

• He was later appointed Viceroy and died at Cochin in 1524.

 

• Gama's three links with India, in 1498, 1502 and 1524, show that statement three is wrong.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gama's second voyage in 1502 was a punitive expedition with a large fleet.

 

• He was helped by a Gujarati merchant, Abdul Majid, in 1498.

 

• His voyage is regarded as the beginning of a European sea-borne trade link to India.

 

• Gama was made Count of Vidigueira by the Portuguese king for his service, and he died at Cochin in December 1524.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 1): Statements 2 and 3 do not fit together, because the false third statement is paired with a true one while the true first statement is left out.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 2): Statements 1 and 3 combine one true fact with the false claim that Gama did not come back, so the pair is flawed.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 3): All three statements would include the incorrect claim of a single voyage, though Gama came again in 1502 and as Viceroy in 1524.

question:
Consider the following statements:

1. Captain William Hawkins was sent by the English company to Jahangir's court.

2. Sir Thomas Roe secured permission for English factories at Agra, Ahmedabad and Broach.

3. Hawkins secured a permanent factory at Surat from Akbar.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Hawkins reached Surat in 1608 and Jahangir's court in 1609 with a letter from King James I (हॉकिन्स 1609 में जहाँगीर के दरबार में)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: Sir Thomas Roe won permission for factories at Agra, Ahmedabad, Baroda and Broach, and Agra became the first inland factory.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: Akbar had already died in 1605, and Jahangir, though first agreeing, later refused the Surat factory because of Portuguese pressure.

 

• Hawkins received the title English Khan and a mansab of 400 but not the trading rights.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The permanent English factory at Surat dates from 1613.

 

• Roe's term at the Mughal court lasted from 1615 to 1619.

 

• James I was the king who wrote to Jahangir through both envoys.

 

• Hawkins stayed at Agra for about two years and married an Armenian lady, a point recorded in his journal.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 2): Statements 2 and 3 pair a true fact with a false one, since Hawkins failed and the Mughal ruler of the time was Jahangir, not Akbar.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 3): Statements 1 and 3 carry the same false claim about Akbar, though Hawkins's mission was in the reign of Jahangir.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 4): Choosing all three accepts that a permanent Surat factory came from Akbar, which is wrong on both ruler and date. It confuses the ruler and the date.

question:
Consider the following statements about the Danes in India:

1. The Danish East India Company was established in 1616.

2. Their first factory was founded at Tranquebar.

3. They sold their Indian settlements to the French in 1845.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: the Danish East India Company was set up in 1616 (डेनिश ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी 1616 में स्थापित)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: the first factory was founded in 1620 at Tranquebar in Tamil Nadu.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: in 1845 the Danes sold all their settlements, including Serampore, to the British, not to the French.

 

• Their headquarters had been moved to Serampore in 1755.

 

• Roe and Hawkins both dealt with Jahangir, which shows that statement three, referring to Akbar, is the odd one out.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Danes were the fourth European power to enter Indian trade.

 

• Serampore later became a centre of Christian missionary and educational work.

 

• The French were still in Pondicherry and Chandernagore in 1845.

 

• Danish missionaries at Tranquebar made the first translation of the New Testament into Tamil in 1715.

 

• The Tranquebar mission press also printed the earliest Tamil books in the Tamil language in the eighteenth century.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 1): Pairing statements 2 and 3 includes the false French buyer and omits the correct year of the company, so it does not match the facts.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 2): Pairing statements 1 and 3 repeats the same mistake about the French purchase even though Tranquebar was undoubtedly a Danish factory.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 3): Taking all three would include the wrong buyer; the sale was made to the British East India Company's government in 1845.

question:
Consider the following statements about the French in India:

1. The French East India Company was established by Colbert.

2. Colbert was a minister of Louis XIV.

3. The first French factory in India was set up at Pondicherry.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: the French company was founded in 1664 by Colbert (फ्रांसीसी कंपनी 1664 में कोल्बर्ट ने बनाई)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: Colbert was a minister under Louis XIV and used state funds for the company.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: the first factory was at Surat in 1668, set up by Francis Caron; Pondicherry came in 1674.

 

• Pondicherry later became the main French base on the Coromandel Coast.

 

• The company started in 1616 and sold out in 1845, a presence of two centuries and more.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The French opened a second factory at Masulipatnam in 1669.

 

• Dupleix became the French governor in 1742 and fought the English in the Carnatic.

 

• The French were the last of the five European powers to arrive.

 

• The French later fought three Carnatic Wars (1746-63) against the English, and their final loss at Wandiwash in 1760 ended their political ambitions.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 2): Pairing statements 2 and 3 accepts that Pondicherry was the first factory, though that came only six years after Surat. The notes record Surat as the earlier site.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 3): Pairing statements 1 and 3 repeats the error about Pondicherry and also leaves out the correct statement about Louis XIV. The statements about the company are sound.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 4): Choosing all three would include the wrong first factory; Surat, not Pondicherry, was the original French base. Pondicherry was developed later.

question:
Consider the following statements about the Dutch in India:

1. The Dutch East India Company was formed in 1602.

2. Their first Indian factory was at Masulipatnam.

3. Cornelis de Houtman led the Dutch to Surat in 1596.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct: the Dutch company was formed in 1602 (डच ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी 1602 में बनी)

 

• Statement 2 is correct: the first Dutch factory in India was at Masulipatnam in 1605.

 

• Statement 3 is incorrect: Cornelis de Houtman reached Bantam in Java in 1596, which was in the East Indies, not Surat.

 

• Surat was later the focus of English and French, and also Dutch, trade in Gujarat.

 

• The French company had a state-run structure under Colbert, in contrast to the private character of the English company.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Dutch also had a fort at Pulicat, called Geldria.

 

• They lost out to the English after the defeat at Bedara in 1759.

 

• Chinsurah passed to the British in 1825 in exchange for Sumatra.

 

• The Dutch were active in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa for saltpetre, opium and textiles, and Clive defeated their forces at Bedara in 1759.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 1): Pairing statements 2 and 3 includes the false Surat claim and leaves out the company date, which makes the pair incorrect.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 3): Pairing statements 1 and 3 adds the same mistake about Houtman's destination, and drops the correct Masulipatnam factory. Houtman never sailed to Gujarat on that voyage.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 4): All three would include the wrong place for Houtman's 1596 voyage, which was Java rather than India. Houtman's voyage ended in Java.

question: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
option_1: Francisco de Almeida - First Portuguese Viceroy
option_3: Nino da Cunha - Capture of Goa
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nino da Cunha - Capture of Goa.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nino da Cunha did not capture Goa; Goa was captured by Albuquerque in 1510, while Cunha moved the capital there in 1530 (नीनो दा कुन्हा ने गोवा नहीं जीता, उसे राजधानी बनाया)

 

• Almeida (1505-09) was indeed the first Viceroy of Portuguese India.

 

• Thomas Best fought the Portuguese at Swally in 1612.

 

• Catherine of Braganza brought Bombay as dowry to Charles II in 1662.

 

• The pair of Almeida and the first Viceroy is correct, as are the Best-Swally and Catherine-Bombay pairs, so only the first pair has the wrong link.

 

• Cunha is known for the transfer of the capital and the Hooghly factory, which makes the Goa capture a clear mismatch.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Cunha also set up a factory at Hooghly in Bengal.

 

• Albuquerque captured Malacca (1511) and Hormuz (1515) too.

 

• The pass-based cartaze system formed part of Portuguese naval policy.

 

• Cunha is better known as the governor who acquired Bassein from Gujarat and fortified Diu.

 

• Albuquerque's other conquests were Malacca (1511) and Hormuz (1515), which formed the basis of the Portuguese eastern empire.

 

• The Portuguese settlement at Hooghly lasted until 1632.

 

NOTE

 

• Francisco de Almeida - First Portuguese Viceroy (Option 1): This pair is correct, because Almeida was the first Viceroy and is linked to the Blue Water Policy, so it cannot be the NOT answer.

 

• Thomas Best - Battle of Swally (Option 2): This pair is correct since Best was the English captain who defeated the Portuguese at Swally, and it leads to the Surat factory in 1613.

 

• Catherine of Braganza - Bombay dowry (Option 4): This pair is correct, as Bombay came to Charles II as part of the marriage settlement with Catherine of Braganza. Nothing in the pair is wrong.

question: The Portuguese 'cartaze' system, enforced by their navy in the sixteenth century, required that
option_1: Indian and Arab merchant ships buy a naval pass to sail in the Indian Ocean
option_2: Indian rulers keep a Portuguese resident at their courts
option_3: Portuguese ships pay customs duty at Calicut
option_4: All European ships sail only through the Cape route
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indian and Arab merchant ships buy a naval pass to sail in the Indian Ocean.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The cartaze was a naval pass that Portuguese authorities compelled Asian merchant ships to buy before sailing in the Indian Ocean, with seizure as penalty (कार्ताज़ — पुर्तगालियों का समुद्री परमिट)

 

• It reflected the Blue Water Policy of Almeida, based on naval supremacy rather than land power.

 

• The system gave the Portuguese revenue and let them control the spice trade.

 

• It angered Arab and Gujarati merchants and Indian rulers, and led to conflict such as the Battle of Diu (1509).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Dutch and English later broke the Portuguese monopoly with stronger fleets.

 

• The Mughal ruler Akbar too bought cartazes for his ships on the Hajj route.

 

• The system was a form of maritime tax on trade rather than a scheme of territorial government.

 

• Portuguese naval patrols off the Malabar coast also tried to prevent the pepper trade with Arab ships, and many Indian vessels were seized for not carrying the pass.

 

NOTE

 

• Indian rulers keep a Portuguese resident at their courts (Option 2): A resident at the court of a ruler is a feature of the Subsidiary Alliance of Wellesley in the early nineteenth century, not of the Portuguese cartaze.

 

• Portuguese ships pay customs duty at Calicut (Option 3): Customs payment at Calicut had no link with the cartaze; the Portuguese were in conflict with the Zamorin, who was hostile to their trade claims.

 

• All European ships sail only through the Cape route (Option 4): The cartaze concerned Asian ships needing a pass, and it did not restrict European routes, since the Cape route was the usual passage for Portuguese ships.
